intro_en: In this lesson you will learn to talk about the past. For example: "it rained yesterday" and "the winter was very cold". Then you will learn to compare things. For example: "a plane is faster than a train", "which of the two do you like?" and "which is the best of all?". You will also learn many new adjectives (describing words). They are about weather, seasons, taste and weight.

g12-1.explanation_en: In Tamil we can say "yesterday, rain" with no verb (நேற்று மழை). In Japanese, you need です. To talk about the past, change です to でした: 昨日は雨でした ("it was rainy yesterday"). For "was not", use じゃありませんでした: 昨日は休みじゃありませんでした. な-adjectives follow the same rule. These are 静か、きれい、にぎやか、便利、有名. They work just like nouns (thing words): 町はにぎやかでした / きれいじゃありませんでした. To ask a question, just add か: でしたか. Learn the four forms together: です / じゃありません / でした / じゃありませんでした.
g12-1.tamil_parallel_en: நேற்று விடுமுறையாக இருந்தது ("Yesterday was a holiday") = 昨日は休みでした. விடுமுறையாக இல்லை ("was not a holiday") = 休みじゃありませんでした. Tamil shows the past with இருந்தது. Japanese shows it with でした.
g12-1.formation_en:
N / な-adj + でした (past, affirmative)
N / な-adj + じゃありませんでした (past, negative); alternative: ではありませんでした
Question: 〜でしたか
g12-1.pitfalls_en: The main mistake is mixing forms, like 雨でしたじゃありません. For "was not", always use じゃありませんでした. Nothing else is right.

g12-2.explanation_en: い-adjectives are not like nouns. They change their own ending for the past, like Tamil verbs do. To make the past, drop the last い and add かった: 寒い → 寒かった ("was cold"). To be polite, add です: 寒かったです. For "was not", change い → くなかった: 寒くなかったです ("was not cold"). Here です itself does not change. So 寒いでした and 寒かったでした are both wrong. Only いい is special: よかったです / よくなかったです. In Tamil, a separate verb shows the time (குளிராக இருந்தது, was cold; குளிராக இல்லை, was not cold). In Japanese, the end of the adjective itself shows the time.
g12-2.tamil_parallel_en: நேற்று குளிராக இருந்தது ("It was cold yesterday") = 昨日は寒かったです. குளிராக இல்லை ("was not cold") = 寒くなかったです. Tamil uses the verb இருந்தது. Japanese changes い → かった / くなかった.
g12-2.formation_en:
い-adj (drop い) + かったです: 暑い → 暑かったです
い-adj (drop い) + くなかったです: 暑い → 暑くなかったです (alternative: 暑くありませんでした)
いい → よかったです / よくなかったです
Question: 〜かったですか
g12-2.pitfalls_en: Tamil speakers often say 寒いでした. That is wrong. でした never goes with an い-adjective. The past of いい is not いかった. It is よかった.

g12-3.explanation_en: To compare two things, use より. It means "than" (-ஐ விட). 飛行機は電車より速いです = "A plane is faster than a train" (விமானம் ரயிலை விட வேகமானது). The word order is the same as Tamil. First comes the topic with は. Then comes the thing you compare with + より (-ஐ விட). The adjective comes at the end. In English you say "more" or "-er". In Japanese you don’t need that. The adjective stays the same. Negatives and questions use the same pattern: 〜より重くないです, 〜より速いですか.
g12-3.tamil_parallel_en: விமானம் ரயிலை விட வேகமானது ("A plane is faster than a train") = 飛行機は電車より速いです. より works just like Tamil -ஐ விட, in the same place.
g12-3.formation_en:
N1 + は + N2 + より + adj + です
N1 + は + N2 + より + い-adj くないです / な-adj じゃありません
g12-3.pitfalls_en: You don’t need words like もっと after より. Don’t try to say "more". Using と, as in N1 と N2 より, is also wrong.

g12-4.explanation_en: To ask "which of the two?", use this pattern: N1 と N2 と どちらが 〜ですか. For example: 夏と冬とどちらが好きですか = "Summer and winter: which do you like?". Don’t drop the second と. People sometimes drop it when they talk, but it appears in the exam. For "which of two", always use どちら (polite). In casual talk, you can say どっち. Use どちら even for people or places. In the answer, use N のほうが 〜です. ほう means "side". 夏のほうが好きです = "I like summer (better)". If both are the same, say どちらも 〜です (both). In Tamil you ask "which of these?" (இதில் எது?). Then you answer "this one" with stress (இது தான்). It is just like that.
g12-4.tamil_parallel_en: கோடையும் குளிர்காலமும், எது பிடிக்கும்? ("Summer or winter, which do you like?") = 夏と冬とどちらが好きですか. கோடை தான் பிடிக்கும் ("I like summer") = 夏のほうが好きです. のほうが adds the same stress as Tamil தான்.
g12-4.formation_en:
N1 + と + N2 + と + どちらが + adj + ですか
Answer: N + のほうが + adj + です
Both: どちらも + adj + です
g12-4.pitfalls_en: When you ask "which of two", don’t use どれ. どれ is for three or more. Use only どちら. In the answer, don’t say 夏がほうが with が. Say 夏のほうが with の.

g12-5.explanation_en: To say "the most" among three or more things, use 一番 (いちばん = "number one, most"). First name the group with N の中で ("among N"). Then say X が 一番 adj です. For example: 飲み物の中でお茶が一番好きです = "Among drinks, I like tea the most". The Tamil "among" ending (-இல், as in பானங்களில், among drinks) is の中で. Tamil "most" (மிகவும் / எல்லாவற்றையும் விட) is 一番. To ask, use a question word + が. Use 何 for things, どこ for places, 誰 for people and いつ for times. Don’t use どちら here. It is only for two. 一番 comes right before the adjective.
g12-5.tamil_parallel_en: பானங்களில் டீ தான் மிகவும் பிடிக்கும் ("Among drinks, I like tea the most") = 飲み物の中でお茶が一番好きです. の中で matches Tamil -களில் ("among"). 一番 matches மிகவும் ("most").
g12-5.formation_en:
N (group) + の中で + 〔何 / どこ / 誰 / いつ〕 + が + 一番 + adj + ですか
Answer: N + が + 一番 + adj + です
g12-5.pitfalls_en: With more than two things, don’t ask with どちら. Use 何 / どこ / 誰 / いつ. Don’t put 一番 at the start of the sentence. Put it right before the adjective.

g12-6.explanation_en: You don’t need to repeat a thing you already talked about. Add の after an adjective to mean "the one". この赤いの = "this red one". 大きいの = "the big one". Tamil does the same with an ending. "The big clock" (பெரிய கடிகாரம்) becomes "the big one" (பெரியது, with -து). An い-adjective takes の directly (軽いの). A な-adjective keeps な before の (きれいなの、静かなの). Remember 私の (mine) from Lesson 2. Here too, の takes the place of a noun. So が, を, は and other particles can come after it: 黒いのを買いました.
g12-6.tamil_parallel_en: சிவப்பானது பிடிக்கும் ("I like the red one") = 赤いのが好きです. Adjective + の works like Tamil adjective + அது / -து ("the ... one").
g12-6.formation_en:
い-adj + の: 大きいの、安いの
な-adj + な + の: きれいなの、便利なの
この / その / あの + adj + の: この赤いの
(+ が / を / は …)
g12-6.pitfalls_en: Don’t forget な after a な-adjective. きれいの is wrong. きれいなの is right. If the listener doesn’t already know the thing, don’t use の. Say the noun itself.

items.L12-q01: 雨 = あめ (மழை, rain). あま is how 雨 is read inside some longer words. On its own it is あめ.
items.L12-q02: 近い = ちかい (அருகில், near). とおい is 遠い (தூரம், far), the opposite. ちがい is wrong because one sound is changed.
items.L12-q03: 冬 = ふゆ (குளிர்காலம், winter). なつ is 夏 (கோடை, summer). ふゆう is wrong because it adds a long sound.
items.L12-q04: A "thick" book = 厚い (தடிமனானது, thick). Three different kanji are read あつい. 暑い is hot weather. 熱い is hot to touch. 厚い is thick.
items.L12-q05: Fast = 速い (வேகம், fast). 早い (Lesson 4) means "early". For the speed of a plane, use 速い. 連 and 束 only look similar.
items.L12-q06: "Very hot" means the sky is clear and sunny = 晴れ (வெயில், sunny). With 雨 or 雪, it would not be hot.
items.L12-q07: "Not heavy" means light → 軽い (இலேசானது, light). 薄い (மெல்லிய, thin) is not about weight.
items.L12-q08: Not hot and not cold means lukewarm → 温い (ぬるい, இளஞ்சூடு, lukewarm). 冷たい is already ruled out.
items.L12-q09: Indian food is spicy = 辛い (காரமானது, spicy). The others (heavy, far, slow) are not about the taste of food.
items.L12-q10: "Very quiet" means there are few people → 少ない (குறைவு, few). 多い (அதிகம், many) is the opposite.
items.L12-q11: "Doesn’t work" means a day off = 休み (விடுமுறை, holiday). The seasons (春、夏) don’t fit here.
items.L12-q12: "The train is faster than the bus" = "the bus is slower than the train". If you swap the nouns before and after より, you must also change the adjective to its opposite.
items.L12-q13: "Not cold" = "it was nice and warm" → 暖かかったです (இதமாக இருந்தது, was warm). 冷たい is for cold things, not for weather.
items.L12-q14: 易しい (எளிது, easy) = 難しくない (கடினமில்லை, not difficult). 厚くない (தடிமனில்லை, not thick) has a different meaning.
items.L12-q15: 雨 (மழை, rain) is a noun, so its past is でした. かったです is only for い-adjectives.
items.L12-q16: For the past of an い-adjective, change い → かったです. Tamil speakers often say 暑いでした. That is wrong. でした does not go here.
items.L12-q17: For "was not" with an い-adjective, use くなかったです. じゃありませんでした is only for nouns and な-adjectives.
items.L12-q18: "Than" = より (-ஐ விட). ほう is used in answers, as のほうが. It doesn’t go after the thing you compare with.
items.L12-q19: "Which of two" = どちら (இரண்டில் எது). どれ is for three or more.
items.L12-q20: "When" in the year = いつ (எப்போது). 一年の中で is a group of many months. どちら is only for two.
items.L12-q21: 黒いの = "the black one" (கருப்பானது). Here の takes the place of かばん. A particle can’t come right after an adjective, so 黒いを is wrong.
items.L12-q22: 日本語は英語より難しいです (ஜப்பானிய மொழி ஆங்கிலத்தை விட கடினம், Japanese is harder than English). The order is: the thing you compare with (英語) + より + adjective + です.
items.L12-q23: The pattern is N1と N2と どちらが 〜ですか. どちらが comes after the second と.
items.L12-q24: 家族の中で誰が一番料理が上手ですか (குடும்பத்தில் யார் மிகவும் நன்றாகச் சமைப்பார்?, who in the family cooks best?). The order is: group (の中で) → question word + が → 一番 → adjective.
items.L12-q25: [1] 晴れ (வெயில், sunny) is a noun, so its past is 晴れでした. [2] 冷たい (குளிர்ச்சி, cold) is an い-adjective, so its past is 冷たかったです. 冷たいでした is wrong. [3] To compare, "than" = より (-ஐ விட).
